declarations.parity_review: Rust requires HTTP 401 for GET state and POST halt/resume without credentials and proves the owner's full before/after state is unchanged.

Rust halts with a reason, checks numeric stopped count and null stop error, reads the same halted state, requires the exact 409 agent_halted/create-thread refusal, resumes and successfully creates a thread record with HTTP 201. No provider turn is launched.
Rust submits a 501-character halt reason, requires HTTP 400 and proves the full control state unchanged. Number/null/array reasons get the same no-mutation check.
Rust sends invalid bearer tokens to refresh, requires HTTP 204 with empty bodies, and verifies no replacement cookie is issued. Invalid cookie refresh is also refused.

Rust persists two proposals then lists exactly two in newest-first identity order, with source thread id/title, priority, due date, serialized tags, null completion time and empty history. Complete listed rows must equal their creation responses.

Rust updates message/status/priority/dueDate/tags and checks null completion, completes from in_progress with exactly one history entry tied to completedAt, reopens with cleared completedAt and retained history, and deletes with an empty persisted list afterwards.
Rust creates a done proposal and requires a completion timestamp and exactly one history entry containing that timestamp and previousStatus:null.
Rust creates a project over an existing disposable folder without .git, attempts assignment, and requires HTTP 400 with the exact PROJECT_NOT_GIT code and details.
Rust requires HTTP 401 for anonymous chat POST, message GET, stream GET, and cancel POST, covering all four protected endpoints.
